test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A water tank can be filled in 19 minutes by using 39 pipes of the same capacity . In how many minutes (rounded off to two decimal places) will the water tank be filled if we use 23 pipes of the same capacity as above?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
Apply the **Inverse Proportion** rule: **M₁ × T₁ = M₂ × T₂**

Where **M** is the number of **pipes** and **T** is the **time** taken.

39 × 19 = 23 × T₂

T₂ = 741 ÷ 23 ≈ 32.22

**∴ The correct answer is 32.22 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of pipes (P₁) = **39 pipes**

Initial time taken (T₁) = **19 minutes**

Final number of pipes (P₂) = **23 pipes**

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Number of Pipes × Time taken

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Capacity of Tank = 39 × 19 = **741 units**

⇒ Required Time (T₂) = Total Capacity ÷ Number of Pipes

⇒ T₂ = 741 ÷ 23

⇒ T₂ = 32.21739...

⇒ T₂ ≈ **32.22 minutes** (rounded off to two decimal places)

**∴ The correct answer is 32.22 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Variation in Work

When the **efficiency** of each unit is constant, the time required is **inversely proportional** to the number of units (pipes/men). If pipes decrease, time increases.

Chain Rule Formula

The general relation is M₁D₁H₁/W₁ = M₂D₂H₂/W₂, where M is power, D/H is time, and W is work.</p
